title: incident-bot: prioritize runbook suggestions using SLO correlation and actionability scoring
author: Priya Nambiar
description:
Motivation: on-call noise and long MTTRs are often caused by low-quality runbook suggestions surfaced by the incident-bot. This PR implements a lightweight scoring pipeline that ranks candidate runbooks by a combination of SLO-correlation, recent success rate (playbook effectiveness), and an actionability heuristic so the bot surfaces higher-quality, high-confidence suggestions first.

What changed: added a new runbook_scoring module that ingests candidate runbook metadata and telemetry signals and returns a normalized score. Hooked scoring into the existing suggestion flow so suggestions are sorted and top-N are shown in the oncall UI and Slack messages. Added feature flag (incident_bot.runbook_priority_scoring) to guard rollout.

Checklist:
- [x] scoring model + unit tests
- [x] integration in suggestion flow
- [x] telemetry (metrics/events) for scoring distribution and top suggestion acceptance
- [x] feature flag + config defaults
- [x] docs: short note in runbooks.md and oncall-helpers.md
- [x] e2e smoke test covering Slack message formatting

Related: builds on work in ENG-2010 (runbook metadata standardization) and ENG-1956 (SLO-correlation metrics).

Notes on rollout: initially enabled for 10% of incidents in prod via feature flag. We will monitor acceptance_rate.runbook_suggestions and mttr.suggested_actions over 2 weeks. If metrics regress beyond threshold, we will rollback the flag.

Implementation details: scoring pipeline uses a simple linear weighting: score = w1 * slo_correlation_score + w2 * playbook_success_rate + w3 * actionability_score + w4 * recency_boost. We persist per-runbook aggregates in the incident-bot metadata store (TTL 30d) and expose metrics: incident_bot.runbook.score_distribution, incident_bot.runbook.top_accept_rate, incident_bot.runbook.scoring_latency_ms. The module is implemented in Python and kept dependency-free (stdlib + existing infra clients).

Migration and backward compatibility: when the feature flag is off, behavior is unchanged. Existing runbook suggestion format is preserved; we only add an optional "score" field. Backfill job not included in this PR; will follow up with a small migration to compute aggregates for high-traffic runbooks.

Links: linear/ENG-2034, docs/runbooks.md#priority-scoring

release_notes: Enhancement: incident-bot now prioritizes runbook suggestions using SLO-correlation and actionability scoring. Feature gated, rolled out at 10% initially. Improves on-call relevance and reduces MTTR by surfacing higher-quality actions.
testing_notes: Unit tests for scoring edge cases included. Integration test covers end-to-end suggestion formatting to Slack. Feature flag ensures safe rollout. Monitor incident_bot.runbook.top_accept_rate and mttr.suggested_actions for regressions.
deployment_instructions: Enable feature flag incident_bot.runbook_priority_scoring in infra/feature_flags to 10% for workspace=prod. Observe metrics for 48h. Increase to 50% after stable. Full rollout contingent on acceptance rate improvement (>5% lift) or no regression in MTTR.
